Event planning · August 25, 2026 · 5 min read

How many glasses do you need per guest at a wedding or event?

A working formula for glassware quantities by service style, plus the breakage allowance that stops you running short on the night.

The working numbers

For a full-service reception with a champagne toast, a cocktail hour and wine with dinner, plan on 2.5 glasses per guest. Split that roughly half champagne flutes for the toast and half all-purpose wine glasses for the rest of the evening. Add a 10% allowance for breakage and loss if the bar is outdoors or if the venue's staff are handling the glassware.

A 200-guest reception therefore needs about 500 pieces: roughly 250 flutes and 250 wine glasses, plus 50 spare. That lands on a comfortable carton count for most of our moulded shapes.

Adjusting by service style

If the venue runs its own bar glassware and you are only supplying the toast, the quantity drops dramatically — this is the single most common reason a first-time buyer over-orders. Ask the venue what they are already providing before you place the order.

  • Champagne toast only, drinks in the venue's own glassware: 1.2 pieces per guest
  • Cocktail hour plus wine with dinner: 2.0 pieces per guest
  • Full reception with toast, cocktail hour and wine service: 2.5 pieces per guest
  • Open bar with a cocktail programme: 3.0 pieces per guest, weighted towards stemless and coupe shapes
  • Beach, pool or garden setting: add 15% rather than 10% for loss

Why the split between shapes matters

It is tempting to buy all champagne flutes because the toast is the photograph you care about. In practice, flutes are poor all-purpose glasses: they hold too little for a wine pour and guests will return to the bar more often. A 50/50 split between flutes and a general wine glass keeps the toast looking right and keeps the rest of the evening working.

If the bar is serving cocktails, swap part of the wine glass allocation for a coupe or a lowball. A ribbed coupe photographs as well as a flute and works for both a cocktail hour and a dessert wine.

Do not forget the rest of the table

Consolidating all of this into one supplier matters more than the unit price. Glassware, buckets and spare stock arriving separately means separate freight, separate delivery windows and a real risk that the spares turn up after the event.

  • One ice bucket per two tables for a chilled service
  • A spittoon or dump bucket if there is a tasting element
  • Water glasses at roughly one per guest, refilled in place
  • Spare flutes for a late toast, kept boxed and unwashed

Questions on this topic

How many glasses do I need for 200 guests?

For a full reception with a champagne toast, cocktail hour and wine service, plan on about 500 pieces — roughly 250 flutes and 250 wine glasses — plus a 10% breakage allowance, so about 550 pieces in total.

Should I buy flutes or wine glasses?

Buy both. A 50/50 split keeps the toast looking right without forcing guests to drink wine from a flute, which pours too small and sends people back to the bar.

How much breakage should I allow for?

Add 10% for an indoor event and 15% for an outdoor, beach or pool setting. Modern moulded drinkware breaks far less than glass, but the allowance covers loss and keeps you from running short.

Can I reuse the glasses for the next event?

Yes, if you specify the right material. Tritan and PP tolerate commercial dishwashing and are designed for repeat use, while PET is the economical choice for single-event service.

How do we convert a guest count into a case quantity?

Convert the guest count into glasses per guest, then into units, then into case packs for the SKUs you selected. Send the guest count, the number of drinks per guest and the SKUs so the case quantity is confirmed against the actual pack size.

Request a quote

Should the keepsake glass be counted separately?

Yes. If the glass leaves with the guest, the keepsake quantity is planned separately from the glasses used during service, because the two are replaced on different cycles.

Weddings and events

How should a breakage allowance be planned?

Plan the allowance from the venue, the surface being used and whether the glass is collected during service. Confirm the venue conditions with us and we will state the quantity basis in the quotation.
